subject: Food Science
title: Water Activity and Shelf Life
description: A fast breakdown of Water Activity and Shelf Life for builders.

hook.text: Honey never spoils—archaeologists found edible honey in 3,000-year-old Egyptian tombs. The secret is extremely low water activity.

buildup.text: Water activity (aw) measures available water for microbial growth on a scale of 0–1. Pure water is 1.0.

discovery.text: Honey has aw of 0.6. Dried pasta: 0.5. Crackers: 0.3. Below 0.6, virtually no pathogens can grow.

twist.text: Water Activity and Shelf Life has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: Controlling water activity is cheaper than refrigeration for developing countries.

punchline.text: Microbes need available water. Lower it below 0.6 and nearly nothing grows.

quiz.question: Why does honey never spoil?
options: Its water activity (0.6) is too low for virtually any pathogen to grow
